input_packet.case_brief: Choose a PhD path while preserving fallback viability and avoiding false precision about outcomes. decision_evaluation
input_packet.anchor_visible_candidate:
I would not choose the hybrid direction yet. Treat two questions as gates, not vibes: does Dr. Silva actually have usable data you can access on a clear timeline, and is your fallback still advisor-backed, resourced, technically ready, identity-coherent, and protected by a stop-loss plan?

Keep the political sequence clean. Talk to your advisor first. Use Dr. Silva only as a low-cost reality check on concrete data access, collaboration depth, and timing. Go to the committee only after you know whether the data path is real and whether your advisor would support the move without quietly pulling you back toward the safer lab path.

For the next two weeks, do dated evidence checks instead of building a finished proposal. Ask what data exists, who controls it, when you could inspect it, what authorship or collaboration terms would look like, and what work would still be yours. In parallel, test whether the fallback path can genuinely carry a dissertation if the Silva path fails.

Do not run all three options in parallel. Do not treat broad PhD success-rate claims as calibrated probabilities for this case; use them only as humility checks. Choose the path only after the Silva/data gate and the fallback gate both have concrete evidence. The best path is not the hottest story; it is the one with a real chance of becoming a finishable PhD.
input_packet.deck_pressure_candidate: Do not choose a dissertation direction yet. Treat the next few weeks as a short, low‑cost test rather than a commitment. The real decision turns on two gates. First, check whether the Silva direction can actually become a dissertation: confirm you can get early data, identify a collaborator who can compensate for the lab’s single‑cell gaps, and get explicit support from your advisor rather than assuming it. Second, keep the fallback alive while you test Silva. It only remains a fallback if your advisor keeps it resourced, available, and ready for you to re‑enter, and if you set a clear stop date with visible conditions for saying no. Coordinate with your advisor before you involve a committee. Run the Silva probe strictly within the short window you define, and make the continuation decision only after you have actual evidence on both gates.

More importantly, the deck pressure introduces a subtle dilution: it softens the gate structure into 'treat the next few weeks as a short, low-cost test rather than a commitment,' which weakens the anchor's sharper 'gates, not vibes' stance and its explicit 'do not run all three options in parallel' boundary. The deck pressure also adds 'coordinate with your advisor before you involve a committee,' which is already present in the anchor's 'talk to your advisor first...go to the committee only after.' The anchor's version is more politically precise and structurally cleaner.
